outcome.title: Persist tenant-access projection state and prove convergence
outcome.bounded: Add a tenant-domain durable-store capability behind `ITenantProjectionStore`, configure its Conversations consumer, expose explicit freshness/sequence/gap state, prove restart and two-replica convergence, and remove the single-replica warning only after those proofs pass.

rollback.boundary: Revert only the durable provider/configuration, Conversations adoption, tests/evidence, Tenants promotion commit, and root gitlink update. Preserve tenant events, public contracts, completed records, other gitlinks, and accepted evidence.

scenarios.given: Given Hexalith.Platform infrastructure and operational policy, its owner-reviewed AD-5 envelope, and additive EventStore and Tenants contracts for durable tenant authorization.
scenarios.when: When contract tests evaluate tenant-segmented storage keys, freshness, sequence progression, fingerprints, pending gaps, and every non-healthy access state.
scenarios.then: Then EventStore owns immutable-envelope extraction, ETag/CAS, retry, replay scheduling, fenced leases, and acknowledgement; Tenants owns the pure transition and projection/checkpoint schema behind ITenantProjectionStore; Conversations configures and consumes those seams without generic Dapr store plumbing. Exact-next events atomically CAS projection and checkpoint. Identical accepted fingerprints are no-ops; accepted-sequence identity conflicts become Corrupt. Older sequences are never reapplied: authoritative-history comparison makes an exact match a no-op, missing or mismatched identity Corrupt, and unavailable verification Unavailable. Only Healthy(lastContiguousSequence) permits authorization; unknown, stale, gapped, corrupt, or unavailable state denies access. The envelope identifies its Architect/Runtime owner, local/CI/staging/production parity and providers, infrastructure responsibilities, state/pubsub/secret/identity dependencies, health/telemetry, backup/rebuild/disaster procedures, operator runbooks, scaling limits, and waiver expiry; only Release accepts capacity or parity waivers. Platform owns physical provider/component selection, injected configuration, declarative subscriptions, identity, telemetry and recovery policy; Conversations follows its enrollment kit and never hardcodes a separate infrastructure binding.

scenarios.given: Given acknowledged tenant events with both authorized and denied outcomes persisted together with sequence and freshness metadata.
scenarios.when: When the Conversations process and any recovery worker restart without tenant-event redelivery and authorization is checked through the consumer.
scenarios.then: Then persisted decisions and sequence/freshness metadata reload identically. Any pending gap remains fail-closed with its immutable expected sequence, monotonic recoveryThrough horizon, and durable per-sequence observed messageId/eventType/payloadFingerprint evidence. Recovery resumes through EventStore under a restart-safe fenced lease and record version; restart cannot discard pending fingerprints or grant authorization before verified Healthy state.

scenarios.given: Given two Conversations replicas sharing the durable tenant projection while Dapr delivers each event to exactly one consumer-group member.
scenarios.when: When concurrent deliveries and reverse-save schedules race against updates, retries, and a recovery horizon extension.
scenarios.then: Then both replicas converge to the same safe access decision and contiguous sequence; neither remains permanently empty or regresses a disable, membership, role, or configuration change. Every future delivery CAS-merges recoveryThrough=max(current, deliveredSequence), retains all observed evidence, treats identical evidence as a no-op, and makes conflicting evidence Corrupt. Recovery CAS-proves an unchanged lease, record version, checkpoint, and horizon with no pending fingerprint before Healthy; otherwise it continues through the enlarged horizon. An expired or superseded worker cannot clear newer state. Acknowledgement follows a durable accepted, duplicate, pending, or corrupt outcome only.

scenarios.given: Given provider and consumer conformance fixtures with duplicate, out-of-order, missing-sequence, store-unavailable, corrupt-record, and tenant-disable inputs.
scenarios.when: When tests execute reverse-save concurrency, equal-sequence mismatch, at least three interleaved future deliveries, concurrent horizon extension, three-total-attempt retry exhaustion, lease expiry and restart, failed and successful recovery, and two-replica schedules.
scenarios.then: Then duplicates are idempotent and every unsafe state is visible with stable content-safe diagnostics and denies authorization. Future deliveries persist immutable expected sequence and monotonically merge the recovery horizon and observed fingerprints without removal or replacement. Authoritative replay validates every observation and applies the same Tenants transition contiguously; missing or conflicting authoritative history becomes Corrupt. Provider/CAS failure or retry exhaustion is retryable and is never acknowledged; provider or exhausted retry state is Unavailable. Only durably committed accepted, duplicate, pending, or corrupt outcomes acknowledge delivery. Queries never schedule, perform, or clear recovery, and Conversations never clears gap/corruption state.

scenarios.given: Given implemented additive Tenants and EventStore seams, Conversations configuration and access adapters, and an accepted operational envelope.
scenarios.when: When the focused Tenants and Conversations projects build and test and public-contract, tenant-safety, restart, and two-replica evidence is compared.
scenarios.then: Then required measured tests have zero failed, skipped, or not-run results; upstream surfaces remain additive, public Conversations contract shape is preserved, and personal tenant data never enters Conversations events or logs. Shared runtime capability remains platform-owned. Remove the single-replica warning only after restart and two-replica convergence proofs pass; local topology cannot substitute for the envelope or a Release-owned capacity/parity waiver.

scenarios.given: Given later approved successor adoption, compatible predecessor evidence, authorized Story 16.1 entry, and five nonempty passing measured scenario results at the committed candidate.
scenarios.when: When the canonical final-record generator supports the adopted successor contract and generates its JSON and deterministic Markdown pair.
scenarios.then: Then the generated summary is 6/6/0/0/0/0 and binds exact root/Tenants gitlinks, source/input/output/schema digests, candidate identity, fault ledger, and the unchanged rollback boundary. Counts, file lists, commits, and verdicts are derived rather than caller-authored. This draft does not claim generator compatibility, verifier availability, owner approval, or permission to start the story; hold remains ACTIVE pending separate decisions.

outcome.title: Make replay time deterministic and missing-index state truthful
outcome.bounded: Derive deterministic v2 replay state and ReplayAnchorAt from validated immutable event inputs, preserve independently generated public observation-time freshness under ProjectionFreshnessV1, eliminate replay clock fallbacks, use the single v2 event-fed Conversation lifecycle/watermark index, and distinguish initialized-empty from missing, erased, rebuilding, corrupt, or unavailable state without query-side repair writes.

rollback.boundary: Revert only timestamp derivation, the lifecycle/watermark addition, read semantics, tests/evidence, and the Story 16.2 record. Preserve event history, public contract shape, Story 16.1 state, and prior proof history.

scenarios.given: Given fixed authoritative histories including participant/file evidence, contract events, position-only events, and missing or invalid event-time/identity cases.
scenarios.when: When materialization validates stream identity, exact persisted payload bytes, selected event time, and duplicate bindings before duplicate suppression.
scenarios.then: Then contract-event identity/time is ConversationEventMetadata.EventId/OccurredAt and position-only identity/time is nonblank persisted ProjectionEventDto.MessageId/Timestamp. Envelope time is diagnostic for contract events and a difference alone is not corruption; aggregate sequence proves contiguity and never supplies alternate identity. The decoder retains position-only identity and selected time. Missing identity, default/invalid time, changed selected time, or conflicting duplicate binding fails closed before suppression. The full duplicate binding includes tenant, conversation, eventType, sequence, serializationFormat, SHA-256(exact persisted payload bytes), and selectedUtcTicks; exact reuse is a no-op and changed reuse is Unavailable/metadata_contradictory. Replay never substitutes UtcNow, Now, or TimeProvider.GetUtcNow(); legacy fallback requires explicit migration authority.

scenarios.given: Given byte-identical authoritative inputs, an adopted AD-8 contract, and two clean rebuilds executed under different runtime clocks.
scenarios.when: When EventStore canonicalizes deterministic v2 replay-state values with fixed JsonSerializerDefaults.Web, compact UTF-8, recursively ordinal-sorted object properties, and explicitly ordinally ordered arrays/collections supplied by Conversations.
scenarios.then: Then canonical deterministic v2 replay-state JSON, ReplayAnchorAt, and ReplayStateHash are byte-identical for identical authoritative inputs, while public observation-time freshness is generated anew, conforms to ProjectionFreshnessV1, is excluded from replay identity, and is tested for semantic invariants rather than byte equality. ReplayAnchorAt is the maximum validated contributing event/lifecycle time. ReplayStateHash is SHA-256 of the exact EventStore canonical value bytes, excluding operational freshness, provider wrappers, ETags, batch IDs, TTL, and the separate coordinated-batch fingerprint. Deserialize-and-canonical-reserialize bytes match and unordered collections without a stable composite key fail before persistence. ProjectionGeneratedAt is the actual completion instant, LastAppliedEventTimestamp is the applicable replay anchor, and LagDuration spans them; generation before the anchor fails closed instead of clamping. This explicitly replaces historical AC-16.2-02 whole-projection-JSON and timestamp byte equality; complete provider documents and observation timestamps may differ. Source-generated API options are not injected into the fixed batch seam; new persistence metadata needs a versioned EventStore API and golden vectors before this story.

scenarios.given: Given never-used and initialized-empty tenants, v1/missing indexes with surviving details, erased state, pending dispatch, gaps, corrupt metadata, mixed generations, unavailable providers, and unauthorized/nonexistent tenants.
scenarios.when: When authorized production queries evaluate the v2 ConversationProjectionIndexReadModel at projection:conversations-index:<tenant-segment> and its lifecycle, watermarks, generation, dispatch references, and rebuild barrier/manifest.
scenarios.then: Then this control index is the sole Conversations lifecycle/watermark authority. Only TenantCreated+Absent creates Ready(empty); Absent/v1 enters Rebuilding, Ready enters Erasing then Erased, and only explicit owner-authorized rebuild can leave Erased through Rebuilding to Ready. Only proven v2 Ready with zero summaries and no pending dispatch maps Current/current with an empty page. v1/Erasing/Erased/Rebuilding maps Rebuilding/rebuilding; lifecycle/source-position gaps map Rebuilding/gap_detected; a missing authorized-tenant record or unavailable provider maps Unavailable/unavailable; corrupt, mixed-generation, or contradictory state maps Unavailable/metadata_contradictory. Unauthorized and nonexistent tenants map non-disclosing Forbidden/forbidden without any index read. A surviving detail cannot prove current-empty.

scenarios.given: Given event-fed lifecycle initialization, live delivery, erase/rebuild intents, durable queued references, and a state-store write ledger around all query paths.
scenarios.when: When lifecycle adapters and coordinators submit intents to ConversationProjectionReadModelWriter and EventStore executes the writer-produced CAS plans while reads run concurrently.
scenarios.then: Then queries perform zero repair writes and never infer lifecycle on read. Only the writer authors transition plans; lifecycle fields and index entries share one CAS boundary. Each erase/rebuild increments generation across detail, dispatch, manifest, watermark, and queued references, and stale-generation mutations are rejected. Erase captures its barrier/deletion manifest, deletes only retiring-generation targets, and retains the control tombstone plus non-payload quarantine references. During Erasing/Erased, deliveries acknowledge only after an authoritative-location reference is durably quarantined and cannot recreate derived content. Rebuild discovers authoritative tenant-scoped streams at B, durably queues later deliveries, proves exact-next per-aggregate sequence through B, drains through captured C, and CAS-cuts over only with complete manifests/watermarks. Post-C deliveries stay queued, same-generation progress alone can merge, and newer watermarks never regress. Numeric EventStore global-position gaps are scan barriers, never tenant-stream contiguity proof.

scenarios.given: Given implemented index/replay changes behind existing public contracts and focused query, freshness, redaction, tenant-isolation, rebuild, and provider conformance lanes.
scenarios.when: When required measured tests execute migration/rebuild/erase races, stale generations, duplicate identity/time conflicts, observation-time invariants, canonical round trips, and query side-effect checks.
scenarios.then: Then public query/freshness contract shape and the existing safe UX/API vocabulary remain unchanged; all required results are nonempty with zero failed, skipped, or not-run. Detail/dispatch/index generations must agree or queries return Rebuilding. Redaction and tenant isolation remain preserved, canonical replay output remains event-derived, and public observation-time freshness follows AD-8 semantics rather than the replaced whole-document byte-equality rule. EventStore retains generic persistence/recovery and canonicalization ownership; Conversations never repairs derived state on read.

scenarios.when: When the canonical generator supports the successor and derives the Story 16.2 JSON/Markdown final record.

Preserve Story 16.1 durable state and prior proof history. The record separates deterministic replay identity from public observation-time freshness. This draft grants no approval or execution authority and remains incompatible with the current generator until explicit adoption.

outcome.title: Diagnose AppHost preflight failures and prove terminal reconciliation live
outcome.bounded: Add stable endpoint-readiness and Dapr control-plane port-collision diagnostics, then prove durable pending work is cleared through the live `project/v2/reconcile` production route and becomes query-visible.

rollback.boundary: Remove only the diagnostics, AppHost fixtures/tests, route assertions, and Story 16.3 record. Preserve the production route, platform hosting ownership, Stories 16.1/16.2, and public contracts.

scenarios.given: Given accepted Stories 16.1/16.2, separately authorized entry, an accepted operational envelope, and an explicit baseline-owner/Architect/Runtime AppHost exemption or relocation amendment.
scenarios.when: When an AppHost resource reports healthy but its named effective endpoint remains unavailable for connection within the bounded readiness policy.
scenarios.then: Then preflight fails before the live lane with stable APPHOST_ENDPOINT_NOT_READY, endpoint identity, and bounded retry advice; diagnostics contain no content or tenant data. The non-packable local fixture remains test infrastructure and cannot assert production-provider parity, baseline conformance, or new runtime authority. The AppHost ownership decision remains pending in this draft.

scenarios.given: Given the effective Dapr control-plane endpoint/port inventory for the isolated live fixture and its provider responsibilities from the operational envelope.
scenarios.when: When one effective Dapr control-plane binding is occupied and the unrelated-port negative case is also exercised.
scenarios.then: Then preflight emits stable DAPR_CONTROL_PLANE_PORT_COLLISION naming the owning endpoint/port before running the lane; unrelated port use does not produce the classification. The fixture restores its own occupied ports and cannot claim environment parity or a capacity waiver through local test topology.

scenarios.given: Given a live, authorized AppHost topology using the production EventStore coordinator and the adopted durable tenant and lifecycle/replay seams.
scenarios.when: When a controlled first Conversations projection failure is induced through production delivery.
scenarios.then: Then durable pending or terminal projection work is observable before retry, while tenant access remains fail-closed and derived-state lifecycle/generation checks remain effective. Evidence binds the live runtime, route/catalog identity, and persisted pending state. Direct handler invocation, reflective worker access, query-triggered recovery, and a second reconciliation implementation cannot establish this proof. EventStore owns durable scheduling and acknowledgement; accepted pending outcomes acknowledge only after durable commit.

scenarios.given: Given the measured durable terminal item from the live first-failure scenario and authenticated access to the production project/v2/reconcile coordinator/module route.
scenarios.when: When a production reconciliation request is observed on the wire and retry executes through the hosted EventStore coordinator into Conversations.
scenarios.then: Then retry clears the durable terminal item exactly once and corrected persisted projection state becomes visible through production queries. Duplicate requests and concurrent newer progress remain idempotent without erasing newer checkpoints, generations, or watermarks; stale/expired workers cannot clear newer state. Existing tenant authorization, lifecycle mappings, and event-identity/time bindings continue to apply. A direct handler result or mock count cannot replace durable end-state and query evidence.

scenarios.given: Given isolated route-removal/fingerprint-drift, duplicate-retry, endpoint-race, effective-port-collision, unavailable-Dapr, and empty-test-selection faults.
scenarios.when: When the production-route live lane and preflight are exercised for each fault with bounded cancellation and captured fixture/port state before and after.
scenarios.then: Then each expected stable failure/blocker is observed with a nonempty ledger, no failed/skipped/not-run required result passes, and fixture files/ports restore. Endpoint and provider faults remain distinct from product failures; environmental inability is BLOCKED. Pending/recovery evidence remains durable and tenant/content-safe, unauthorized calls never gain access, and recovery cannot bypass AD-6 fences, AD-7 generation/lifecycle rules, or AD-8 identity/time validation. Required operational health/telemetry and recovery/runbook expectations remain owned by the envelope; tests cannot invent a waiver.

scenarios.given: Given compatible accepted predecessors, a resolved AppHost ownership decision, separate scoped execution authorization, adopted successor contracts, and five passing current measured results.
scenarios.when: When the canonical generator supports the successor and derives the Story 16.3 JSON/Markdown pair.
scenarios.then: Then the summary is 6/6/0/0/0/0 and binds AppHost/runtime identities, production route proof, safe diagnostics, exact candidate/root gitlinks, input/output/fault digests, and unchanged rollback. Preserve production routes, platform hosting ownership, Stories 16.1/16.2, public contracts, and prior evidence. This draft claims no owner approval, accepted envelope/waiver, AppHost exemption, runtime verification, generator compatibility, or execution authority; hold remains ACTIVE.

Duplicate/conflict schedules are separate branches from the enlarged gap.

Only entry advances generation. Every stage retains exact index and logical component contents. A stale entry plan is rejected after newer completion. No runtime provider implementation is claimed.

concurrentRecovery.description: Controlled capture v1: each staleAttempts storedBefore is an independent reset/fork from newerStored; storedAfter proves preservation. Current clearance and duplicate retry are a separate positive branch. Time is checked within each branch, not chronologically across distinct controls. Superseded-lease and stale-checkpoint branches independently isolate only the named fence with all other fences current and an unexpired lease.
